title: Bring all docs up to date for the 1.0.0 release

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The S104-S123 arc changed the command surface and behavior a lot -- render-failure policy and `--strict`, the render merge driver plus `setup-git`, claims (`start`/`release`, the CLAIM column, `--json` `claim`/`in_work_elsewhere`), `list` column labels and hidden-count, the merge-in-progress guard, the code/worktree mismatch warning, and the `verify` driver warning. Docs were updated piecemeal per slice; before 1.0.0 they need one holistic pass so the command reference, examples, and narrative are accurate and complete, with nothing stale or missing (e.g. `setup-git`, `release`).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `README.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/agents.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `AGENTS.md`
- `src/slicer/ai.py` (the `ai instructions` / `ai skill` text, if it enumerates commands or workflow)
- a doc-coverage test if one is warranted

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. Every subcommand slicer registers appears in the docs command reference (add a test that diffs the parser's command list against the documented one, or verify by review).
2. The doc `slicer ...` examples still parse (existing `test_ai` example-parser test stays green), and no doc names a removed flag.
3. `ai instructions`/`ai skill` describe the current implement loop and commands.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Audit each document against the current command surface. Add the missing commands (`setup-git`, `release`, and any others), refresh the command table/list, update examples, and make the merge-driver, claim, `--strict`, and guard workflows read coherently as one story. Reconcile any drift between README, getting-started, agents.md, AGENTS.md, and the `ai` text. Prefer a review-plus-small-test approach over inventing new prose.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Docs reviewed and consistent; the command reference matches the parser; examples parse; the suite and `slicer check` pass.
